description: The study's theoretical framework is Bahr's deconstructive approach, in which students' academic pathways through higher education are examined to understand their dynamic interaction with institutional integration and progress toward academic goals.
title: Bahr's deconstructive analysis approach

description: The article operationalizes dialogue through four Bakhtin-inspired themes used both to train teachers and to analyze noticing utterances.
title: Bakhtinian dialogic framework of four interconnected themes — voices, expanding the dialogue, inter-animation, and relations

description: Because unbalanced training data produce systematic over- or under-estimation of code prevalence, the article recommends balancing the presence and absence of a code in training data.
title: Balanced training-set design for machine coding

description: The paper recommends that studies using student achievement outcomes generally aim to collect and use baseline data, because analyses using more than one wave of data typically have much greater statistical power than posttest-only analyses.
title: Baseline covariate adjustment in education randomized trials

description: A Bayesian framework for comparing ordinal categorical education distributions: first order stochastic dominance and a restricted two-category form for education levels; generalized Lorenz dominance, the Cowell–Flachaire and Jenkins indices, and a poverty-style headcount index for inequality.
title: Bayesian dominance-based framework for comparing ordinal categorical education distributions

description: The authors state a limitation of their classical procedures: single-subject designs are very short time series and this presents a problem in estimating the parameters in the autoregressive process assumed for the errors.
title: Bayesian estimation of autoregressive parameters in short single-subject time series

description: Bayesian Networks are presented as both a specification language and a computational mechanism with practical value in designing group and learning support systems: they have \"been frequently used to build student models (Millán et al., 2010) and for assessment (Almond et al., 2015)\".
title: Bayesian Networks for student modelling, assessment, and collaborative learning theory

description: A novel methodological approach in which each yoked participant observes the responses of an \"ideal Bayesian learner\" personalized to have that participant's individual prior beliefs.
title: Bayesian Yoking Procedure
